question: Why are VIC & TAS claims taking longer to close since June 2026?

sql:
WITH source AS (
    SELECT c.*, p.channel, p.metro,
           coalesce(pay.paid, 0) AS paid_to_date,
           coalesce(pay.paid, 0) + c.reserve_amount AS incurred,
           c.close_date - c.report_date AS days_to_close
    FROM claims c
    JOIN policies p USING (policy_id)
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT claim_id, sum(amount) AS paid FROM claim_payments GROUP BY claim_id
    ) pay USING (claim_id)
)
SELECT CAST(date_trunc('month', report_date) AS DATE) AS period, region, median(days_to_close) FILTER (WHERE status = 'closed') AS value
FROM source
WHERE report_date >= DATE '2026-01-01'
  AND report_date <= DATE '2026-09-30'
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY ALL

report.interpretation: Cycle time is the agreed metric: median days from report date to close date, for closed claims only, grouped by report month. I compared VIC & TAS claims reported in Jun–Jul 2026 with those reported Jan–May 2026. I left out Aug and Sep because those claims are still open, so the closed-only median looks faster than it will end up.
report.answer: The slowdown is real. VIC & TAS median cycle time rose from 26 days (claims reported Jan–May 2026) to 33 days (Jun–Jul). The monthly medians were 33 in June and 34 in July, against 25–28 in each earlier month. The other regions stayed roughly flat. The data points to a staffing change as the likely cause. Three of the region's eight adjusters left in June (ADJ-010 on 1 Jun, ADJ-011 on 10 Jun, ADJ-012 on 20 Jun). Together they had handled about 11 claims a month each. Their work moved to the remaining five adjusters, who went from roughly 10–13 claims a month each to roughly 16–22. Total regional volume was steady at about 94–107 claims a month. Every remaining adjuster's median rose, for example ADJ-015 from 23 to 31.5 days and ADJ-016 from 32 to 39 days. The slowdown is not tied to one cause of loss, state, channel or repair shop. Every shop's median rose by about 7–11 days, and claims with no shop, mostly home claims, rose from 38 to 53 days. This is an association with the timing of the departures, not proof of cause. I didn't test wait times, reassignment dates or handoff delays.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adjuster departures and the resulting workload concentration
hypotheses.evidence: Three of eight adjusters left in June. Their workload moved to five colleagues, whose claims per month rose by about 60–100%, and every remaining adjuster's median rose.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Change in mix of cause, state or channel
hypotheses.evidence: Medians rose across collision, storm, theft, third-party property and water damage, in both VIC and TAS, and in all three channels. Glass was flat at 7 to 8 days.
All major shops, preferred and non-preferred, slowed by a similar 7–11 days.
The claims table has no duplicate rows. Aug and Sep were excluded from the comparison because their open claims bias the closed-only median down.
I did not query weather_events. Volume was steady, which makes a surge less likely.

data_quality_issues.issue: Aug and Sep 2026 reports are incomplete. 43 of 111 Aug claims and 63 of 75 Sep claims are still open.
data_quality_issues.impact: The closed-only median for those months looks faster than it will end up (28.5 days for Aug and 9 for Sep), so they were excluded from the comparison.

proposed_actions.title: Review VIC & TAS adjuster capacity
proposed_actions.reason: Three of eight adjusters left in June and the remaining five carry about 16–22 claims a month each. Operations should consider backfilling or rebalancing.

open_questions: Did the reassigned claims wait in a queue before being picked up? I didn't have the data to measure this.
Were any VIC & TAS claims reassigned from the departed adjusters, and when?
I didn't check weather_events for a storm or hail spike in Jun–Jul.
